correctness.rationale: For each horizontal column the exact height transition is \(\mathbf1_{h\prime\geq h-1}+(-1)^{\xi_i}\mathbf1_{h\prime\geq h}\), with heights bounded by \(0\leq h_i\leq n-i\). The first column contributes \(1+(-1)^{\xi_0}\), proving exactly half the Fourier multipliers vanish. For \(\xi_0=0\) all later transitions are nonnegative: a forced all-down history contributes 2, while any later positive sign provides a distinct flat-step history contributing 4, proving unique sharp positive gap 2. Every incidence vector has a constructive path, making zero frequency the unique largest coefficient R_n. Fourier diagonalization gives rank/nullity \(2^{n-1}\), range independence of the first coordinate, and sharp nonzero spectral condition number \(R_n/2\). The extracted integer verifier passed 33,021 coefficient comparisons and histogram equalities through n=14; finite checks are only corroboration.

The most relevant indexed published results and previously documented mathematical statements concern other path encodings, different statistics, or interval-set kernels. No broader theorem in checked material was shown to imply the conclusion. This is bounded-priority novelty, not a proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The diagonal-column incidence law of classical Schröder paths is a natural push-forward retaining positional information lost by standard univariate enumeration. The theorem supplies a complete all-size classification of its Fourier kernel, identifies the exact recoverable quotient and an independent fair coordinate, and proves a sharp nonzero spectral gap and conditioning law. These are structural signal-recovery properties, not a single small numerical case, unmotivated parameter slice, or formal restatement of the total Schröder count.
